【发掘 agent 本轮输出】:
【状态】: 有发掘空间

【前置调研发现】
- [CoRL 2026 Call for Papers](https://www.corl.org/contributions/call-for-papers) (CoRL 2026): CoRL 是 Conference on Robot Learning，明确要求 "submissions should focus on a core robotics problem"，鼓励真实机器人实验或可迁移至真实机器人的仿真实验。本 proposal 关于多语言 LLM 的跨语言知识传导性，与机器人学习零相关。**这是致命的 venue mismatch。**
- [On the Entity-Level Alignment in Crosslingual Consistency (arXiv:2510.10280)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10280) (2025): 核心发现 entity alignment 与 cross-lingual consistency 的 Pearson r > 0.7；提出 SubInj/SubSub 推理时干预方法，仅通过在 prompt 中注入英文实体名即可获得 +14-32% recall 和 +17-44% consistency 提升。这是 EACA 最直接的 "trivial alternative" 威胁。
- [CCL-XCoT (EMNLP Findings 2025, arXiv:2507.14239)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.14239): 句子/段落级对比 CPT + XCoT prompting，hallucination 降低 62%。确认为句子级粒度，无实体锚定。
- [FactNet (arXiv:2602.03417, Feb 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03417): 1.7B atomic facts，316 Wikipedia editions，grounding precision 92.1%。资源真实可用，pipeline 可行性有保障。
- [CLiKA (NAACL 2024, arXiv:2404.04659)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04659): 定义 XRR metric，发现 multilingual pretraining 和 instruction tuning 均未实质性改善 conductivity (XRR < 0.01)，但未提出具体解决方案。这一 open problem 确实悬而未决。
- [Bandarkar et al. (arXiv:2603.17070, March 2026)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.17070): 确认 script match 是跨语言知识迁移失败的首要预测因子（~13% gap），entity priming 实验直接支持"实体映射是跨 script 瓶颈"的假设。
- [DCO (arXiv:2603.04678, March 2026)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.04678): DPO-inspired 后处理一致性优化，互补而非竞争方向。
- 调研总结: 该领域当前研究者主要从两个角度突破——(1) 粒度下沉（从句子级到实体级）识别跨语言不一致性的 mechanistic bottleneck，(2) script barrier 作为新发现的主要障碍需要专门处理。但目前尚无工作将实体级对比学习嵌入 decoder LLM 的 CPT 中；推理时干预方法（SubInj）已取得显著成效，训练时方法需要明确说明其相对于推理时干预的不可替代价值。

---

【发掘点 1】
- 维度: 前提假设质疑（致命问题）
- 内容: **CoRL 2026 是 Conference on Robot Learning（机器人学习会议）**，其 Call for Papers 明确要求论文"focus on a core robotics problem"并鼓励报告真实机器人实验。本 proposal 的主题是多语言 LLM 中的跨语言知识传导性（cross-lingual knowledge conductivity），属于纯 NLP/多语言 AI 研究，与机器人学习无任何交叉。投稿 CoRL 几乎必然被 desk reject。正确的目标 venue 应为 ACL、EMNLP、NAACL、COLM 或 ICLR 等接受 NLP/LLM 研究的会议。
- 价值: 这是决定中稿概率的前置条件——idea 质量再高，venue 不对则概率为零。
- 调研依据: [CoRL 2026 Call for Papers](https://www.corl.org/contributions/call-for-papers) 明确限定 scope 为 robot learning。

【发掘点 2】
- 维度: trivial alternative 威胁
- 内容: SubInj（arXiv:2510.10280）通过推理时在 prompt 中注入英文实体名，即可获得 +14-32% recall 和 +17-44% consistency 提升，计算成本几乎为零。EACA 需要 ~1100-1550 H100 小时的训练才能实现训练时实体对齐。Proposal 当前仅以"EACA aims to achieve this alignment at training time"一句带过，未充分回答 **为什么训练时对齐是不可替代的**。这是审稿人几乎必问的问题。建议在核心 claim 中明确阐述训练时对齐相对于推理时干预的结构性优势，例如：(a) 推理时干预需要已知目标实体的英文翻译，这在 open-ended generation 中不可用（用户无法预知模型将生成哪些实体）；(b) 推理时干预无法改变模型内部的知识表征结构，只能 patch 表层行为——CLiKA 区分的 consistency vs. conductivity 恰好对应这一区别；(c) SubInj 在 conductivity (XRR) 指标上的表现未被报告，可能仅改善 consistency 而非 conductivity。如果 EACA 能在 XRR 上取得突破（而非仅在 consistency metric 上），其相对于 SubInj 的价值定位会极为清晰。
- 价值: 直接强化核心 claim 的必要性论证，堵住审稿人"为什么不直接用 SubInj"的质疑，同时锐化 EACA 的 novelty 定位（targeting conductivity, not just consistency）。命中 Novelty + Significance。
- 调研依据: [arXiv:2510.10280](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10280) 的 SubInj 方法及其 +14-32%/+17-44% 结果。

【发掘点 3】
- 维度: novelty 锐化
- 内容: Proposal 声称 6 项 novelty，但其中多项是标准工程选择而非概念创新：(3) inverse-frequency weighting 是常见的 class-imbalance 技术；(4) gradient conflict monitoring 使用的 PCGrad/GradNorm 是现成的多任务学习工具；(6) "直接 targeting CLiKA's conductivity gap with script-stratified evaluation" 是评估策略而非方法创新。真正的核心 novelty 是一个清晰的 insight：**factual knowledge 在 LLM 中以实体为原子单位存储和检索（由 Entity Lens、CLM-Bench、arXiv:2510.10280 多方佐证），因此跨语言知识对齐应在实体级而非句子级进行对比学习——这是将 contrastive CPT 从语句粒度下沉到知识原子粒度的范式转变**。建议将 novelty claim 压缩为 1 个核心 insight + 2 个使其成立的关键技术设计（structured KG grounding via QIDs、script-aware augmentation），而非堆叠 6 个平行 claim。
- 价值: 审稿人面对 6 个 "novelty" 时会感到 diluted——每个都不够重要。压缩为 1 个锐利的核心 claim 后，novelty 的说服力会显著提升。命中 Novelty。
- 调研依据: 基于领域整体趋势判断——近期高影响力论文（CCL-XCoT、Liu & Niehues）均以一个清晰的核心 insight 作为卖点，而非堆叠技术 contribution。

【发掘点 4】
- 维度: significance 提升
- 内容: Proposal 将 significance 完全锚定在技术指标（XRR < 0.01）上，缺乏对 **为什么解决 conductivity 问题对领域真正重要** 的论证。XRR < 0.01 意味着什么？它意味着在一种语言中学到的知识几乎无法被另一种语言检索——多语言 LLM 实际上在不同语言间维护着近乎独立的知识存储。这对以下场景有深远影响：(a) 低资源语言的知识获取——如果 Swahili 用户无法访问用英文训练的知识，则多语言模型对这些用户的价值大打折扣；(b) 事实一致性的信任问题——同一模型对同一事实在不同语言给出不同答案会严重损害可信度；(c) multilingual AI safety——知识不连通意味着在某些语言上更容易被诱导产生错误信息。建议在 framing 中增加 1-2 句对 real-world impact 的阐述，将技术问题（XRR < 0.01）与实际应用需求连接。
- 价值: 从"这是一个有趣的技术 gap"升级为"这是一个影响多语言 AI 公平性和可信度的关键问题"。命中 Significance。
- 调研依据: 基于领域整体趋势判断——CLiKA 原文和 Bandarkar et al. 都隐含了这些 implications 但未充分展开；近期 ACL 2025 cultural knowledge asymmetry 论文也指向同一方向。

【发掘点 5】
- 维度: 核心 claim 强化
- 内容: Proposal 的逻辑链条中有一个 gap：r > 0.7 的 entity alignment 与 consistency 相关性来自 **观测性研究**（arXiv:2510.10280），证明的是"entity alignment 好 → consistency 高"的相关关系，而非因果关系。EACA 的核心假设是"通过对比学习强制 entity alignment → 将提升 conductivity"，这需要从 correlation 跳到 intervention 的因果推断。建议在 proposal 中明确承认这一 gap，并将 Phase 0 pilot 定位为对这一因果假设的直接检验：如果 entity cosine similarity 提升但 XRR 未改善，则说明训练时对齐改变的是表征空间结构而非模型实际检索知识的方式。这种诚实的 framing 反而会增强 claim 的可信度——审稿人更信任承认假设边界的作者。
- 价值: 将核心 claim 从"entity alignment 一定改善 conductivity"软化为"entity alignment 是 conductivity 的最强预测因子，EACA 是首个通过 causal intervention (训练时对比学习) 检验这一假设的工作"。这实际上使 claim 更强——无论实验结果正负，论文都有 contribution。命中 Novelty + Significance。
- 调研依据: [arXiv:2510.10280](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10280) 的相关性分析是 observational 而非 interventional 的。

Sources:

- [CCL-XCoT (arXiv:2507.14239)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.14239)
- [FactNet (arXiv:2602.03417)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03417)
- [CLiKA (arXiv:2404.04659)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04659)
- [Bandarkar et al. (arXiv:2603.17070)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17070)
- [DCO (arXiv:2603.04678)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04678)

【状态】: 发现致命缺陷

【前置调研发现】
- **CCL-XCoT** (EMNLP Findings 2025, [aclanthology](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-emnlp.93/)): 实验在 Gemma-7B/LLaMA-3.1-8B 上进行，baselines 包括 +SFT、+CL（sentence-level contrastive）、+CCL（curriculum contrastive）；评估中文/马来语/泰米尔语的 hallucination-free rate；使用 LoRA layers 9-19/11-22；报告了 up to 62% hallucination reduction。
- **CLiKA** (NAACL 2024, [arXiv:2404.04659](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04659)): 定义 Performance/Consistency/Conductivity 三层评估框架；Conductivity 用 XRR（Cross-Retrieval Ratio）度量，基于 fictional knowledge 注入英语后测试跨语言检索；评估 BLOOM、LLaMA 等多模型；发现 XRR < 0.01。
- **Liu & Niehues** (ACL 2025, [arXiv:2502.14830](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14830)): 在 LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct/Qwen2.5-7B 上进行；middle-layer (layer 16/32) 上 mean-pooled sentence contrastive alignment；LoRA rank 8；评估 slot filling (+1.5 F1)、MT (+1.5 BLEU)；ablation 包括 layer selection、alignment language choice、LoRA rank。
- **FactNet** (arXiv:2602.03417, Feb 2026): 1.7B atomic facts, 3.01B evidence pointers, 316 Wikipedia editions；grounding precision 92.1%；提供 FactNet-Bench (KGC/QA/Fact Checking)；数据已在 HuggingFace 公开。
- **BMLAMA-53** (EMNLP 2023): 3000 queries across 53 languages 的 multi-parallel factual consistency benchmark；近期工作(2025-2026)仍在使用，但也有 MLC (exact Top-1 match) 等替代指标被提出。
- **CoRL 2026** ([corl.org](https://www.corl.org/contributions/call-for-papers)): Conference on Robot Learning，主题覆盖 imitation learning、RL for robots、sim-to-real、robot perception/manipulation/locomotion、learning-based planning；要求 submissions "focus on a core robotics problem"；abstract deadline May 26, 2026, paper deadline May 29, 2026。
- **On the Entity-Level Alignment in Crosslingual Consistency** (arXiv:2510.10280): 发现 entity alignment 与 cross-lingual consistency 的 Pearson r > 0.7；提出 SubInj 方法；>99% consistent facts 显示 successful entity alignment。
- 调研总结: 该 proposal 所在领域（cross-lingual knowledge consistency/conductivity）的实验标准包括：多 baseline 对比（sentence-level contrastive、standard CPT、entity augmentation）、多 benchmark 评估（BMLAMA-53、TyDiQA、XRR）、script-grouped analysis、ablation 覆盖核心组件。**但 CoRL 2026 是机器人学习会议，与此 NLP 研究方向完全不匹配，投稿可行性为零。**

---

【缺陷 1】
- 类别: 可行性问题
- 问题: **投稿目标会议 CoRL 2026（Conference on Robot Learning）与 proposal 研究方向完全不匹配。** CoRL 的 Call for Papers 明确要求 "submissions should focus on a core robotics problem and demonstrate the relevance of proposed models, algorithms, datasets, and benchmarks to robotics"，主题覆盖 imitation learning、RL for robots、sim-to-real、robot manipulation/locomotion、learning-based planning 等。本 proposal 是纯 NLP/CL 研究（cross-lingual entity-level contrastive alignment for multilingual knowledge conductivity），不包含任何 robotics component。即使实验设计完美无缺，该论文也会在 CoRL 被 desk reject 或在审稿第一轮因 out-of-scope 被拒。
- 严重度: 不可补救（方向性致命）
- 补救方案: **无法通过修改实验设计补救——这是投稿策略层面的根本错误。** 建议更换目标会议为 NLP/CL 主流会议，如 **EMNLP 2026**（Call for Papers 已开放，涵盖 Multilingual NLP、Knowledge Representation）、**ACL 2026**、**NAACL 2026**、或 **COLM 2026**（如关注 language model 方向）。如果确实希望投稿 robotics 相关会议，则需要从根本上重新设计研究问题，将 cross-lingual knowledge conductivity 应用于 robotics 场景（如多语言机器人指令理解），但这实质上是一个完全不同的项目。
- 调研依据: CoRL 2026 官方 Call for Papers（https://www.corl.org/contributions/call-for-papers）明确的 scope 定义。

---

**以下缺陷假设投稿目标更正为 NLP/CL 主流会议（如 EMNLP/ACL），在此前提下评估实验设计层面的完备性：**

---

【缺陷 2】
- 类别: 评估方案缺陷
- 问题: **CLiKA XRR 评估协议与 EACA 训练流程的整合未说明。** Proposal 将 CLiKA 的 XRR 列为核心评估指标之一（"CLiKA's XRR metric (to directly measure conductivity improvement)"），但 XRR 的测量需要先在英语中注入 fictional knowledge（人工虚构的实体-关系知识），然后测试其他语言是否能检索到这些知识。这要求在 EACA continued pretraining 之后，再进行一轮 fictional knowledge injection training。但 proposal 没有说明：(1) fictional knowledge injection 是否与 entity contrastive loss 兼容——虚构实体没有 Wikidata QID，如何处理？(2) injection 后是否需要冻结 EACA 的 LoRA weights？(3) XRR 评估的 compute budget 是否已计入总资源估算中？这一遗漏可能导致核心 claim（"improve conductivity as measured by XRR"）无法被直接验证。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) 在 Approach 或 Evaluation 部分明确 XRR 评估协议：在 EACA CPT 完成后，按照 CLiKA 原始设定进行 fictional knowledge injection（使用 standard fine-tuning 而非 contrastive loss，因为虚构实体无 QID），然后测量跨语言检索率；(2) 将此 injection step 的 compute 纳入资源估算（估计额外 ~20-30 H100 hours）；(3) 作为 ablation 之一，对比 EACA+injection vs. baseline+injection，确保 conductivity 提升来自 EACA 而非 injection 本身的变化。
- 调研依据: CLiKA (NAACL 2024) 的 XRR 评估协议要求 fictional knowledge injection 作为前置步骤。

【缺陷 3】
- 类别: 实验设计不足
- 问题: **缺少统计显著性分析和多 seed 实验。** Proposal 的 go/no-go criteria（"entity cosine similarity improvement ≥ 0.05, BMLAMA-53 consistency improvement ≥ 2 points"）和最终评估均未提及多次随机种子运行、confidence intervals 或 significance tests。在 cross-lingual factual consistency 领域，提升幅度通常较小（CLiKA 显示 XRR < 0.01，EACA 的期望提升可能也是个位数百分点），若不报告方差和显著性，审稿人很可能质疑观察到的提升是否来自随机波动。近期 ACL/EMNLP 论文普遍要求至少 3 seeds + 标准差报告。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) Phase 0 pilot 和 full training 均运行至少 3 个不同随机种子；(2) 所有表格报告 mean ± std；(3) 对核心对比（EACA vs. CCL-XCoT, EACA vs. standard CPT）进行 paired bootstrap 或 McNemar 检验；(4) 将多 seed 的 compute overhead (~2x-3x Phase 0 cost, i.e., 额外 ~260-390 H100 hours) 纳入资源估算。注意：如果 3 seeds 对 full training 不可承受（每次 ~800-1100 H100 hours），至少对 Phase 0 做多 seed，对 full training 用 1 seed + bootstrap resampling on evaluation。
- 调研依据: 基于领域实验规范判断。Liu & Niehues (ACL 2025) 报告了多组实验的标准差；CCL-XCoT 在多语言上报告变化范围。ACL/EMNLP reviewing guidelines 普遍强调 reproducibility 和 variance reporting。

【缺陷 4】
- 类别: baseline 不足或过时
- 问题: **缺少一个关键的 ablation baseline：frequency-weighted data selection only（无 contrastive loss）。** Proposal 的核心贡献之一是 inverse-frequency weighting，但当前实验设计无法隔离这一因素的贡献。具体来说，EACA 同时引入了 (a) entity-level contrastive loss, (b) FactNet-grounded data (naturally entity-centric), (c) inverse-frequency weighting。如果只对比 EACA vs. standard CPT，审稿人无法判断提升来自 contrastive alignment 还是来自更好的数据选择（entity-centric + frequency-weighted sampling）。现有 ablation 列表中有 "frequency weighting on/off" 但没有 "entity-centric data selection + frequency weighting WITHOUT contrastive loss"——即用同样的 FactNet entity-fact data 做 standard NTP，只是没有 contrastive objective。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: 新增一个 baseline: **FactNet-NTP**——使用完全相同的 entity-centric FactNet data（带 [ENT] markers）和相同的 inverse-frequency weighting 进行 standard CPT（仅 NTP loss，无 contrastive），以隔离 contrastive alignment 的独立贡献。这是验证 "entity-level contrastive loss is what improves conductivity, not just better data curation" 的必要对照。Compute cost: 与一次 standard CPT 等同（~100-150 H100 hours for Phase 0 scale）。
- 调研依据: 基于领域实验规范判断。在 contrastive learning 文献中，隔离 data curation effect 和 loss function effect 是标准做法（参见 Robinson et al. ICLR 2021 中对 data distribution vs. loss function 的讨论）。

【缺陷 5】
- 类别: 评估方案缺陷
- 问题: **monolingual capability regression 评估不够全面。** Proposal 提到 "no TyDiQA degradation beyond 1 point" 作为 go/no-go criterion，以及 15% general-domain replay 防止 catastrophic forgetting，但 TyDiQA-GoldP 仅覆盖 QA 能力的一个维度。对于 continued pretraining 方法，审稿人通常期望更全面的通用能力回归测试——如 MMLU（或其多语言版本 M-MMLU）、ARC、HellaSwag 等——以确保 contrastive loss 没有损害模型的 general reasoning 和 instruction following 能力。CCL-XCoT 在其评估中也包含了通用能力对比。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: 在评估 suite 中增加至少 2 个通用能力 benchmark：(1) **MMLU / M-MMLU** (general knowledge and reasoning)；(2) **HellaSwag 或 ARC** (commonsense reasoning)。报告 EACA vs. base model 在这些指标上的变化，确保 degradation 在可接受范围内（< 1-2 points）。这些评估的 compute overhead 很小（几 GPU-hours），不影响总资源预算。
- 调研依据: CCL-XCoT (EMNLP Findings 2025) 的实验设计包含通用能力评估；continued pretraining 领域的审稿标准普遍要求证明方法不损害已有能力。

【缺陷 6】
- 类别: 可行性问题
- 问题: **Ablation 数量与 compute budget 之间存在张力。** Proposal 列出了 11+ 个 ablation 维度（entity-level vs. sentence-level, contrastive vs. masking, transliteration, frequency weighting, type-aware negatives, language count, layer selection, joint vs. alternating, gradient mitigation (3 variants), contrastive pair construction, K_min threshold），每个维度至少需要一次独立训练运行。即使仅在 Phase 0 scale (500M tokens) 执行，每个 ablation ~100-130 H100 hours，11 个维度至少 ~1100-1430 H100 hours——已经接近整个项目的 total budget。Proposal 给 ablation 分配的预算仅 90-165 H100 hours，远远不够。

- 类别: 评估方案缺陷
- 问题: **缺少 open-ended generation 质量评估。** 当前评估 suite（BMLAMA-53 probe-based, TyDiQA extractive QA, X-CODAH multiple-choice, XRR retrieval-based）偏重于 probe/structured evaluation，缺少对 free-form factual generation 的评估。对于一个修改了 decoder LLM 表示空间的 CPT 方法，审稿人可能关心：在开放式事实问答中，模型是否真正在不同语言中生成一致的事实答案？LiveCLKTBench 部分覆盖了这一点，但 proposal 未说明其评估形式（是 free-form 还是 structured）。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) 明确 LiveCLKTBench 的评估形式——如果是 free-form generation，则已部分覆盖；(2) 增加 FActScore（Factuality Assessment with Atomic Claims）或类似 factuality metric 对 EACA 模型 vs. baseline 的 free-form 生成输出进行评估，覆盖至少 Tier 1 + 1 个 Tier 2 语言；(3) 如果 compute 紧张，可将此作为 full training 后的补充评估而非 Phase 0 必须项。
- 调研依据: 基于领域实验规范判断。近期 factual consistency 研究（如 DCO, arXiv:2603.04678）在评估中包含 free-form generation metrics。

【缺陷 8】
- 类别: 可行性问题
- 问题: **Tier 3 语言 Khmer (KM) 的数据可行性风险较高。** Proposal 估算 Khmer 仅有 ~12K Wikipedia articles，FactNet yield rate 0.36 下估计 5K-25K entity-fact pairs，接近甚至可能低于 10K minimum threshold。且 Khmer 不在 DaMuEL 覆盖范围内，需完全依赖 Wikipedia wikilinks extraction pipeline，其覆盖率仅 ~50-60%。Khmer Wikipedia 的 entity linking 质量未知，可能存在大量 QID 缺失。虽然 proposal 有 contingency plan（替换为 Bengali/Tagalog/Hausa），但执行替换会引入时间风险（需重新跑 preprocessing + coverage audit）。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) 将 contingency language selection 前置到项目启动阶段——在 preprocessing pipeline 开始的第一周就并行跑 KM + BN + TL 的 coverage audit，而非等 KM 审计失败后再启动替代方案；(2) 考虑将 **Bengali (BN)** 直接替换 Khmer 作为 Tier 3 代表（~157K Wikipedia articles，远高于 KM 的 ~12K，且使用独立 script Bengali script，仍满足跨 script 多样性需求）；(3) 若保留 KM，明确设定 early termination criterion：若 KM entity-fact pairs < 8K（低于 10K threshold 的 80%），自动触发替换。

- 问题: **CLiKA XRR 评估协议与 EACA 训练流程的整合未说明。** Proposal 将 CLiKA 的 XRR 列为核心评估指标之一（"CLiKA's XRR metric (to directly measure conductivity improvement)"），但 XRR 的测量需要先在英语中注入 fictional knowledge（人工虚构的实体-关系知识），然后测试其他语言是否能检索到这些知识。这要求在 EACA continued pretraining 之后，再进行一轮 fictional knowledge injection training。但 proposal 没有说明：(1) fictional knowledge injection 是否与 entity contrastive loss 兼容——虚构实体没有 Wikidata QID，如何处理？(2) injection 后是否需要冻结 EACA 的 LoRA weights？(3) XRR 评估的 compute budget 是否已计入总资源估算中？这一遗漏可能导致核心 claim（"improve conductivity as measured by XRR"）无法被直接验证。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) 在 Approach 或 Evaluation 部分明确 XRR 评估协议：在 EACA CPT 完成后，按照 CLiKA 原始设定进行 fictional knowledge injection（使用 standard fine-tuning 而非 contrastive loss，因为虚构实体无 QID），然后测量跨语言检索率；(2) 将此 injection step 的 compute 纳入资源估算（估计额外 ~20-30 H100 hours）；(3) 作为 ablation 之一，对比 EACA+injection vs. baseline+injection，确保 conductivity 提升来自 EACA 而非 injection 本身的变化。
- 调研依据: CLiKA (NAACL 2024) 的 XRR 评估协议要求 fictional knowledge injection 作为前置步骤。

【缺陷 3】
- 类别: 实验设计不足
- 问题: **缺少统计显著性分析和多 seed 实验。** Proposal 的 go/no-go criteria（"entity cosine similarity improvement ≥ 0.05, BMLAMA-53 consistency improvement ≥ 2 points"）和最终评估均未提及多次随机种子运行、confidence intervals 或 significance tests。在 cross-lingual factual consistency 领域，提升幅度通常较小（CLiKA 显示 XRR < 0.01，EACA 的期望提升可能也是个位数百分点），若不报告方差和显著性，审稿人很可能质疑观察到的提升是否来自随机波动。近期 ACL/EMNLP 论文普遍要求至少 3 seeds + 标准差报告。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) Phase 0 pilot 和 full training 均运行至少 3 个不同随机种子；(2) 所有表格报告 mean ± std；(3) 对核心对比（EACA vs. CCL-XCoT, EACA vs. standard CPT）进行 paired bootstrap 或 McNemar 检验；(4) 将多 seed 的 compute overhead (~2x-3x Phase 0 cost, i.e., 额外 ~260-390 H100 hours) 纳入资源估算。注意：如果 3 seeds 对 full training 不可承受（每次 ~800-1100 H100 hours），至少对 Phase 0 做多 seed，对 full training 用 1 seed + bootstrap resampling on evaluation。
- 调研依据: 基于领域实验规范判断。Liu & Niehues (ACL 2025) 报告了多组实验的标准差；CCL-XCoT 在多语言上报告变化范围。ACL/EMNLP reviewing guidelines 普遍强调 reproducibility 和 variance reporting。

【缺陷 4】
- 类别: baseline 不足或过时
- 问题: **缺少一个关键的 ablation baseline：frequency-weighted data selection only（无 contrastive loss）。** Proposal 的核心贡献之一是 inverse-frequency weighting，但当前实验设计无法隔离这一因素的贡献。具体来说，EACA 同时引入了 (a) entity-level contrastive loss, (b) FactNet-grounded data (naturally entity-centric), (c) inverse-frequency weighting。如果只对比 EACA vs. standard CPT，审稿人无法判断提升来自 contrastive alignment 还是来自更好的数据选择（entity-centric + frequency-weighted sampling）。现有 ablation 列表中有 "frequency weighting on/off" 但没有 "entity-centric data selection + frequency weighting WITHOUT contrastive loss"——即用同样的 FactNet entity-fact data 做 standard NTP，只是没有 contrastive objective。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: 新增一个 baseline: **FactNet-NTP**——使用完全相同的 entity-centric FactNet data（带 [ENT] markers）和相同的 inverse-frequency weighting 进行 standard CPT（仅 NTP loss，无 contrastive），以隔离 contrastive alignment 的独立贡献。这是验证 "entity-level contrastive loss is what improves conductivity, not just better data curation" 的必要对照。Compute cost: 与一次 standard CPT 等同（~100-150 H100 hours for Phase 0 scale）。
- 调研依据: 基于领域实验规范判断。在 contrastive learning 文献中，隔离 data curation effect 和 loss function effect 是标准做法（参见 Robinson et al. ICLR 2021 中对 data distribution vs. loss function 的讨论）。

【缺陷 5】
- 类别: 评估方案缺陷
- 问题: **monolingual capability regression 评估不够全面。** Proposal 提到 "no TyDiQA degradation beyond 1 point" 作为 go/no-go criterion，以及 15% general-domain replay 防止 catastrophic forgetting，但 TyDiQA-GoldP 仅覆盖 QA 能力的一个维度。对于 continued pretraining 方法，审稿人通常期望更全面的通用能力回归测试——如 MMLU（或其多语言版本 M-MMLU）、ARC、HellaSwag 等——以确保 contrastive loss 没有损害模型的 general reasoning 和 instruction following 能力。CCL-XCoT 在其评估中也包含了通用能力对比。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: 在评估 suite 中增加至少 2 个通用能力 benchmark：(1) **MMLU / M-MMLU** (general knowledge and reasoning)；(2) **HellaSwag 或 ARC** (commonsense reasoning)。报告 EACA vs. base model 在这些指标上的变化，确保 degradation 在可接受范围内（< 1-2 points）。这些评估的 compute overhead 很小（几 GPU-hours），不影响总资源预算。
- 调研依据: CCL-XCoT (EMNLP Findings 2025) 的实验设计包含通用能力评估；continued pretraining 领域的审稿标准普遍要求证明方法不损害已有能力。

【缺陷 6】
- 类别: 可行性问题
- 问题: **Ablation 数量与 compute budget 之间存在张力。** Proposal 列出了 11+ 个 ablation 维度（entity-level vs. sentence-level, contrastive vs. masking, transliteration, frequency weighting, type-aware negatives, language count, layer selection, joint vs. alternating, gradient mitigation (3 variants), contrastive pair construction, K_min threshold），每个维度至少需要一次独立训练运行。即使仅在 Phase 0 scale (500M tokens) 执行，每个 ablation ~100-130 H100 hours，11 个维度至少 ~1100-1430 H100 hours——已经接近整个项目的 total budget。Proposal 给 ablation 分配的预算仅 90-165 H100 hours，远远不够。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) **分级优先化 ablation**：将 ablations 分为 P0（必须做，直接支撑核心 claim）和 P1（nice-to-have，如审稿人要求再补）。P0 应包括：entity-level vs. sentence-level（核心假设）、contrastive vs. masking-based、transliteration on/off、frequency weighting on/off、FactNet-NTP baseline（缺陷4）。P1 包括：type-aware vs. random negatives、K_min variants、gradient mitigation variants、joint vs. alternating、layer selection（已在 Phase 0 sweep 中覆盖）。(2) **修正 ablation compute budget**：P0 ablations (5-6 个) 在 Phase 0 scale 需要 ~500-780 H100 hours，总预算应上调至 ~1600-2100 H100 hours。(3) 部分 ablation 可通过 smaller scale (250M tokens, 3 languages) 执行以节省 compute。
- 调研依据: 基于领域实验规范判断。Liu & Niehues (ACL 2025) 在 ablation 中优先覆盖 layer selection 和 alignment language choice 等核心维度，而非穷举所有可能变体。

【缺陷 7】
- 类别: 评估方案缺陷
- 问题: **缺少 open-ended generation 质量评估。** 当前评估 suite（BMLAMA-53 probe-based, TyDiQA extractive QA, X-CODAH multiple-choice, XRR retrieval-based）偏重于 probe/structured evaluation，缺少对 free-form factual generation 的评估。对于一个修改了 decoder LLM 表示空间的 CPT 方法，审稿人可能关心：在开放式事实问答中，模型是否真正在不同语言中生成一致的事实答案？LiveCLKTBench 部分覆盖了这一点，但 proposal 未说明其评估形式（是 free-form 还是 structured）。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) 明确 LiveCLKTBench 的评估形式——如果是 free-form generation，则已部分覆盖；(2) 增加 FActScore（Factuality Assessment with Atomic Claims）或类似 factuality metric 对 EACA 模型 vs. baseline 的 free-form 生成输出进行评估，覆盖至少 Tier 1 + 1 个 Tier 2 语言；(3) 如果 compute 紧张，可将此作为 full training 后的补充评估而非 Phase 0 必须项。
- 调研依据: 基于领域实验规范判断。近期 factual consistency 研究（如 DCO, arXiv:2603.04678）在评估中包含 free-form generation metrics。

【缺陷 8】
- 类别: 可行性问题
- 问题: **Tier 3 语言 Khmer (KM) 的数据可行性风险较高。** Proposal 估算 Khmer 仅有 ~12K Wikipedia articles，FactNet yield rate 0.36 下估计 5K-25K entity-fact pairs，接近甚至可能低于 10K minimum threshold。且 Khmer 不在 DaMuEL 覆盖范围内，需完全依赖 Wikipedia wikilinks extraction pipeline，其覆盖率仅 ~50-60%。Khmer Wikipedia 的 entity linking 质量未知，可能存在大量 QID 缺失。虽然 proposal 有 contingency plan（替换为 Bengali/Tagalog/Hausa），但执行替换会引入时间风险（需重新跑 preprocessing + coverage audit）。
- 严重度: 可补救
- 补救方案: (1) 将 contingency language selection 前置到项目启动阶段——在 preprocessing pipeline 开始的第一周就并行跑 KM + BN + TL 的 coverage audit，而非等 KM 审计失败后再启动替代方案；(2) 考虑将 **Bengali (BN)** 直接替换 Khmer 作为 Tier 3 代表（~157K Wikipedia articles，远高于 KM 的 ~12K，且使用独立 script Bengali script，仍满足跨 script 多样性需求）；(3) 若保留 KM，明确设定 early termination criterion：若 KM entity-fact pairs < 8K（低于 10K threshold 的 80%），自动触发替换。
- 调研依据: FactNet (arXiv:2602.03417) 报告的 low-resource yield rate (0.36)；DaMuEL 的 53 语言覆盖列表不含 SW/YO/KM。

---

**总结：** 本 proposal 的实验设计在 NLP 领域标准下是相当全面和深思熟虑的——baseline 选择覆盖了核心对比、ablation 设计系统性强、script-grouped analysis 是重要亮点。但存在一个**致命的可行性缺陷**（CoRL 是机器人学习会议，与此 NLP 研究完全不匹配），以及 7 个可补救的实验设计缺陷（XRR 协议整合、统计显著性、data-curation baseline 隔离、monolingual regression、ablation compute budget、open-ended generation 评估、Tier 3 语言风险）。**如果将投稿目标更正为 NLP 主流会议（EMNLP/ACL/NAACL），并完成上述 7 项补救，该 proposal 的实验设计可达到 top-venue 门槛。**

1	# Entity-Anchored Contrastive Alignment for Cross-Lingual Knowledge Conductivity
2	
3	## Description
4	EACA is a continued pretraining method that introduces InfoNCE contrastive loss on entity-span hidden states alongside standard next-token prediction, targeting entity-level cross-lingual knowledge conductivity — a capability that CLiKA (NAACL 2024) established is not substantially improved by existing multilingual pretraining or instruction tuning (XRR < 0.01). Unlike CCL-XCoT (sentence/paragraph-level contrastive CPT) and Liu & Niehues (ACL 2025, sentence-level middle-layer contrastive fine-tuning), EACA anchors contrastive pairs to Wikidata QIDs using FactNet's 1.7B entity-grounded atomic facts, operating at the entity level — the granularity empirically shown to be the bottleneck for cross-lingual consistency (entity alignment correlates at r > 0.7 with consistency, arXiv:2510.10280). This extends KBioXLM's (EMNLP Findings 2023) precedent of multi-granularity entity alignment in multilingual pretraining from encoder-based masking objectives in a specialized domain to explicit contrastive alignment in decoder-only LLMs for general-domain conductivity. Entity spans are marked with LEIA-style [ENT]/[/ENT] tokens using DaMuEL (12.3B QID-annotated tokens across 53 languages) as the primary annotation source for 10 of 13 target languages, supplemented by a Wikipedia wikilinks-to-QID extraction pipeline for the 3 uncovered Tier 3 languages (SW/YO/KM) and mReFinED entity linking for non-hyperlinked mention gap-filling, with 1.5-2 weeks budgeted for preprocessing. Representations are extracted via mean-pooling at middle layers (~layer 16, validated via Phase 0 sweep). The proposal explicitly addresses the script barrier identified by Ifergan et al. (NAACL Findings 2025) and Bandarkar et al. (arXiv:2603.17070): script similarity dominates representation sharing (~37.6% same-script CKR vs. <10-20% cross-script), but entity priming disproportionately helps cross-script transfer, motivating entity-level alignment as targeting the right bottleneck. Cross-script QID pairs receive transliteration-augmented entity markers (e.g., [ENT]北京 (Beijing)[/ENT]), inspired by TransliCo (ACL 2024), with mandatory script-grouped evaluation (same-script vs. cross-script gains). 6	## Core Problem
7	Can entity-level contrastive alignment — anchored to Wikidata QIDs and grounded in FactNet's structured atomic facts — improve cross-lingual knowledge conductivity (as defined by CLiKA's XRR metric, Gao et al. NAACL 2024) more effectively than sentence/paragraph-level contrastive continued pretraining (e.g., CCL-XCoT) or sentence-level middle-layer alignment (Liu & Niehues, ACL 2025)? CLiKA established that neither multilingual pretraining nor instruction tuning substantially improves conductivity, with XRR scores below 0.01 for most non-English languages. EACA hypothesizes that this conductivity barrier persists because prior methods align at sentence/document granularity — conflating entity-specific factual knowledge with syntactic and discourse-level variation — whereas factual knowledge is inherently structured around entities (subject-property-object triples). A critical complication, identified by Ifergan et al. (NAACL Findings 2025) and Bandarkar et al. (arXiv:2603.17070), is that script similarity is the dominant factor in cross-lingual representation sharing: high behavioral consistency does not imply shared internal representation for cross-script language pairs, and script match — not language family — is the primary predictor of knowledge transfer failure. Crucially, however, Bandarkar et al.'s entity priming experiment shows that providing source-language entity names disproportionately improves cross-script transfer, directly implicating entity-level mapping failure as the mechanism behind the script barrier. This suggests that entity-level contrastive alignment targets the right bottleneck, but that cross-script entity alignment requires additional support (e.g., transliteration augmentation) beyond what same-script entity alignment needs. EACA therefore addresses a two-level problem: (1) entity-level alignment as the fundamental unit of factual knowledge transfer, and (2) script-aware strategies to bridge the representation gap across writing systems.

9	## Opportunity
10	CCL-XCoT (EMNLP 2025 Findings) demonstrates that contrastive continued pretraining reduces cross-lingual hallucination by up to 62% but operates at sentence/paragraph granularity with parallel text. Liu & Niehues (ACL 2025) show that middle-layer contrastive alignment (layer 16 of 32 in LLaMA-3-8B) significantly improves cross-lingual transfer for downstream tasks, but again at sentence-level granularity and for task-specific fine-tuning rather than factual consistency. CLiKA (NAACL 2024) reveals a critical gap: existing multilingual pretraining and instruction tuning improve surface-level consistency but fail to improve knowledge conductivity (XRR < 0.01), suggesting that fundamentally different alignment granularity is needed. Meanwhile, FactNet (arXiv:2602.03417, Feb 2026) provides 1.7B entity-grounded atomic facts across 316 Wikipedia editions with Wikidata QID linking — enabling entity-level contrastive pairs grounded in structured knowledge. Entity Lens (BlackboxNLP 2025) confirms that decoder LLMs develop entity-specific internal mechanisms to represent multi-token entities. Liu et al. (EMNLP 2025 Findings) show that cross-lingual transfer is frequency-driven, with low-frequency facts benefiting most. Critically, recent evidence from entity-level alignment analysis (Liu, Wang et al., arXiv:2510.10280) demonstrates that cross-lingual factual consistency correlates strongly with entity alignment (Pearson r > 0.7), with over 99% of consistent facts exhibiting successful entity alignment — providing direct empirical motivation for entity-level rather than sentence-level contrastive objectives. Marco et al. ('Unveiling LLMs', arXiv:2404.03623) further establish that factual knowledge about subject entities concentrates in middle layers (L5-L21 for LLaMA-2-7B). KBioXLM (EMNLP Findings 2023) provides an important precedent: it demonstrated that multi-granularity knowledge alignment (entity masking, relation masking, passage relation prediction) during continued pretraining of XLM-R yields +20 F1 points on cross-lingual zero-shot biomedical tasks, establishing entity-anchored alignment as effective — but using masking-based reconstruction on encoders rather than contrastive loss on decoder LLMs, and targeting downstream task transfer rather than factual conductivity. Ifergan et al. (NAACL Findings 2025) reveal a deeper challenge: using knowledge editing as a probe for representation sharing, they find script similarity is the dominant factor (same-script CKR ~37.6% in Mistral; cross-script <10-20%), and that behavioral consistency diverges sharply from representation sharing for cross-script pairs. Bandarkar et al. (arXiv:2603.17070, March 2026) confirm this with regression analysis showing script match as the primary predictor after controlling for model capability and question difficulty (~13% accuracy gap), but critically, their entity priming experiment shows that providing source-language entity names disproportionately improves cross-script questions — directly implicating entity mapping as the bottleneck. TransliCo (ACL 2024) demonstrates that transliteration-based contrastive learning bridges script barriers using only 5% of training data on encoders. DaMuEL (2023) provides 12.3B tokens with QID-linked entity annotations across 53 languages, enabling efficient preprocessing for 10 of EACA's 13 target languages. The opportunity is to combine these insights — entity-level anchoring + structured knowledge grounding + middle-layer extraction + inverse-frequency weighting + script-aware strategies — into a contrastive CPT method that targets the specific granularity (entities), representation layer (middle), data regime (low-frequency facts), and script barriers where current methods demonstrably fall short.

12	## Related Work / Landscape
13	The cross-lingual factual consistency landscape spans several complementary approaches. CCL-XCoT (EMNLP 2025 Findings) is the primary baseline, employing InfoNCE symmetric contrastive loss during continued pretraining with a sentence-to-paragraph curriculum on Gemma-7B and LLaMA-3.1-8B using LoRA on layers 9-19/11-22, reducing hallucination by 62%, but operating at sentence/paragraph granularity without entity grounding or frequency weighting. Liu & Niehues (ACL 2025) represent the closest methodological precedent for contrastive alignment: they apply contrastive loss on mean-pooled sentence representations at middle layers (specifically layer 16 of 32 for LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct) during task-specific fine-tuning with LoRA (rank 8), demonstrating +1.5 F1 on slot filling and +1.5 BLEU on MT across 35 languages — however, they use sentence-level alignment with alternating (not joint) task/alignment training, target downstream task transfer rather than factual consistency, use parallel text rather than structured knowledge, and include no frequency weighting. EACA differentiates from Liu & Niehues on five axes: (1) entity-level rather than sentence-level granularity, (2) continued pretraining for factual consistency rather than task-specific fine-tuning, (3) FactNet-grounded contrastive pairs rather than parallel text, (4) joint NTP+contrastive objective rather than alternating training, and (5) inverse-frequency weighting for underrepresented facts. KBioXLM (Geng et al., EMNLP Findings 2023, arXiv:2311.11564) is an important precedent for multi-granularity entity-anchored alignment in multilingual pretraining. It performs continued pretraining on XLM-R using three alignment objectives grounded in UMLS biomedical knowledge: entity masking (code-switching entity mentions across EN-CN and predicting masked entity tokens via MLM cross-entropy), relation masking (masking relation tokens in subject-predicate-object triples), and passage relation prediction (3-way classification on aligned EN-CN Wikipedia passages). KBioXLM achieves +20 F1 points on cross-lingual zero-shot biomedical NER/RE. EACA extends this paradigm along four dimensions: (a) decoder-only LLMs vs. encoder (XLM-R), requiring contrastive loss on hidden states rather than masking-based reconstruction, since decoder LLMs lack bidirectional context for effective mask prediction; (b) general domain vs. biomedical, using FactNet's 1.7B facts across 316 editions vs. UMLS's specialized ontology; (c) explicit contrastive alignment (InfoNCE) vs. implicit alignment through masking, directly optimizing cross-lingual entity representation similarity rather than relying on the prediction bottleneck; (d) conductivity metric (CLiKA's XRR) vs. downstream task transfer, targeting the specific capability that prior methods fail to improve. CLiKA (Gao et al., NAACL 2024) provides the diagnostic framework: they define knowledge conductivity as the Cross-Retrieval Ratio (XRR) — retrieving knowledge learned in one language using another — and find that neither multilingual pretraining nor instruction tuning substantially improves XRR (scores < 0.01 for most non-English languages), with no concrete solutions proposed. The entity-level alignment analysis (Liu, Wang et al., arXiv:2510.10280) provides strong empirical support: cross-lingual consistency correlates with entity alignment at r > 0.7, and their SubInj method yields +14-32% recall and +17-44% consistency gains, but only at inference time; EACA aims to achieve this alignment at training time. On the script barrier dimension, Ifergan et al. ('Beneath the Surface of Consistency', NAACL Findings 2025, arXiv:2408.10646) demonstrate via knowledge editing probes on 7 decoder LLMs (7B scale) that script similarity is the dominant factor in cross-lingual knowledge representation sharing (CKR): same-script Latin pairs show ~37.6% average CKR in Mistral, while cross-script pairs show <10-20% transfer; crucially, they find that high behavioral consistency (CKC) does not imply shared representation for cross-script pairs, with E[NCL] consistently exceeding E[NTL]. Even targeted language extension pretraining achieves only marginal cross-script CKR improvement. Bandarkar et al. ('Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts', arXiv:2603.17070, March 2026) confirm via regression analysis on ECLeKTic and MultiLoKo that script match — not language family — is the primary predictor of knowledge transfer failure (~13% accuracy gap), but their entity priming experiment reveals that providing source-language entity names disproportionately improves cross-script questions, directly implicating entity mapping as the cross-script bottleneck. TransliCo (Liu et al., ACL 2024, arXiv:2401.06620) addresses script barriers through transliteration contrastive modeling (TCM), fine-tuning Glot500-m on 5% of data with Latin transliterations as contrastive targets, producing Furina which outperforms Glot500-m on cross-script zero-shot transfer — but operates on encoders at sentence level without entity grounding. Transliteration-based post-training alignment (Moosa et al., EMNLP Findings 2024, arXiv:2406.19759) achieves up to 50% improvement on cross-script English-centric transfer with even larger gains for non-English sources. EACA incorporates this insight by adding transliteration-augmented entity contrastive pairs for cross-script language combinations as a complementary mechanism. NeighXLM (EMNLP 2025 Findings) introduces neighbor-augmented contrastive pretraining for low-resource languages without parallel data, but targets general cross-lingual transfer rather than entity-specific factual consistency. PreAlign (EMNLP 2024) uses code-switching pretraining with word-level alignment but lacks entity anchoring. CrossIC-PT (EMNLP 2025) interleaves bilingual Wikipedia content without entity-level grounding. LEIA (ACL Findings 2024) inserts English entity names with [translate]/[/translate] markers during continued pretraining of decoder LLMs, improving cross-lingual transfer but without contrastive loss or frequency weighting. EntityCS (EMNLP Findings 2022) performs entity-centric code switching with Wikidata but is limited to encoder-only models. Entity Lens (BlackboxNLP 2025) reveals that decoder LLMs develop entity-specific mechanisms to represent and manipulate multi-token entities via task vectors. The middle-layer factual knowledge claim is supported by Liu & Niehues (ACL 2025) showing layer 16 of 32 has strongest cross-lingual retrieval alignment, and Marco et al. (arXiv:2404.03623) demonstrating via dynamic knowledge graphs that middle layers (L5-L21) encode comprehensive factual knowledge while late layers show 90%+ degradation. ELO (arXiv:2601.03648, Jan 2026) demonstrates efficient layer-specific optimization with 6.46x speedup from selective middle-layer updates. FactNet (arXiv:2602.03417) provides 1.7B entity-grounded facts across 316 Wikipedia editions with significant coverage skew. CLM-Bench (arXiv:2601.17397) shows edit vectors are nearly orthogonal across languages, further motivating entity-level alignment. DCO (arXiv:2603.04678, March 2026) proposes DPO-inspired post-hoc consistency optimization, complementary to pretraining-time methods. Veitsman et al. (arXiv:2603.18863, March 2026) find that sentence-level contrastive alignment fails for token-level tasks in XLM-R encoders, supporting entity-level approaches for entity-centric tasks. Cultural knowledge asymmetry research (ACL 2025) confirms that frequency drives cross-lingual transferability.

15	## Approach
16	EACA adds an InfoNCE contrastive loss on entity-span hidden states to the standard next-token prediction (NTP) objective during continued pretraining. The method comprises five integrated components: entity preprocessing, entity-level contrastive alignment, script-aware augmentation, stratified batch construction, and joint optimization with gradient monitoring.
17	
18	**1. Entity Preprocessing Pipeline.** Entity boundary annotation uses a two-stage pipeline. Stage 1 (primary): DaMuEL (2023), which provides 12.3B QID-annotated tokens across 53 languages (CC BY-SA), is used directly for the 10 target languages it covers (EN/ZH/JA/DE/AR/HI/TR/ID/VI/TH). DaMuEL provides start/end token indices per entity mention with Wikidata QID links, extracted from Wikipedia wikilinks and expanded via lemmatization and alias matching (~17% recall gain over raw wikilinks). Stage 2 (Tier 3 gap-filling): For the 3 Tier 3 languages not covered by DaMuEL (SW/YO/KM), a lightweight Wikipedia wikilinks extraction pipeline resolves hyperlinks to QIDs via Wikidata sitelinks (~50-60% mention coverage). mReFinED (EMNLP Findings 2023), which is 44-60x faster than comparable entity linkers, is applied as a second pass on high-resource languages to annotate non-hyperlinked entity mentions where higher recall is needed. Entity boundaries are marked with LEIA-style [ENT]/[/ENT] tokens around linked mentions. Preprocessing budget: 1.5-2 weeks engineering time, ~2-4 GPU-days on A100 for mReFinED gap-filling, ~24-48 CPU-hours for wikilinks extraction across Tier 3 languages. This pipeline is on the critical path and must complete before Phase 0.
19	
20	**2. Entity-Level Contrastive Alignment.** Entity representations are extracted via mean-pooling over hidden states within the [ENT]...[/ENT] span at a designated middle layer (defaulting to layer 16 for 32-layer models based on Liu & Niehues' ACL 2025 finding and Marco et al.'s analysis; validated via Phase 0 sweep over layers 12-20), with loss propagation blocked on boundary markers themselves. Contrastive pairs are constructed per QID from FactNet: positive pairs consist of atomic fact descriptions for the same QID across languages, while negatives come from different QIDs within the same batch (detailed in Component 4). Inverse-frequency weighting assigns higher contrastive loss weight to facts with lower cross-lingual FactNet coverage, directly targeting low-resource facts where CLiKA's conductivity analysis shows the largest gap.
21	
22	Theoretical motivation for entity-level granularity: Three converging lines of evidence support entity-level over sentence-level contrastive alignment for factual consistency: (1) Entity alignment analysis (arXiv:2510.10280) demonstrates Pearson r > 0.7 between entity alignment and cross-lingual consistency, with >99% of consistent facts showing successful entity alignment — establishing entities as the bottleneck for consistency; (2) CLM-Bench's finding that cross-lingual edit vectors are nearly orthogonal implies that factual knowledge editing, which operates at entity-level (subject-property-object triples), requires entity-aligned representations rather than sentence-aligned ones; (3) CLiKA's failure result — that sentence/document-level pretraining and instruction tuning do not improve conductivity — suggests that coarser-grained alignment conflates entity-specific factual knowledge with syntactic and discourse-level variation, diluting the alignment signal.
23	
24	**3. Script Barrier Mitigation.** EACA's 13 target languages span ~7 scripts (Latin: EN/DE/TR/ID/VI/SW/YO; CJK: ZH/JA; Arabic: AR; Devanagari: HI; Thai: TH; Khmer: KM). Ifergan et al. (NAACL Findings 2025) demonstrate that cross-lingual representation sharing (CKR) clusters strongly by script family (~37.6% same-script CKR vs. <10-20% cross-script in Mistral-7B), and Bandarkar et al. (arXiv:2603.17070) confirm script match as the primary predictor of transfer failure (~13% gap). This poses a genuine risk that entity-level contrastive alignment may primarily improve same-script entity alignment while showing limited gains for cross-script pairs. However, two findings provide grounds for cautious optimism: (a) Bandarkar et al.'s entity priming experiment shows source-language entity names disproportionately improve cross-script transfer, implicating entity mapping — not script-level representation — as the cross-script bottleneck for factual knowledge; (b) TransliCo (ACL 2024) demonstrates that transliteration-based contrastive learning bridges script barriers on encoders using only 5% of training data. EACA therefore incorporates a script-aware augmentation strategy: for cross-script QID pairs (e.g., EN-ZH, EN-AR, EN-HI, EN-TH, EN-KM), entity mentions in non-Latin scripts are supplemented with Latin transliterations appended within the [ENT] boundary (e.g., [ENT]北京 (Beijing)[/ENT]), providing a lexical bridge for the contrastive objective. This is tested as an ablation (EACA vs. EACA+translit) to isolate the contribution of transliteration augmentation beyond entity-level alignment. The evaluation plan includes mandatory script-grouped analysis: same-script entity alignment gains (Latin-Latin, CJK-CJK) vs. cross-script gains (Latin-CJK, Latin-Arabic, Latin-Devanagari, etc.), reporting both entity cosine similarity and downstream factual consistency metrics separately for each script-pair category. If Phase 0 reveals that cross-script entity alignment gains are <50% of same-script gains despite transliteration augmentation, this will be explicitly reported as a limitation and the analysis will quantify what fraction of EACA's overall conductivity improvement comes from same-script vs. cross-script alignment.
25	
26	**4. Stratified Batch Construction with Type-Aware Hard Negatives.** Effective contrastive learning is highly sensitive to negative quality (Robinson et al., ICLR 2021). EACA uses stratified mini-batching: each batch contains K_batch = 128-256 unique QIDs, with all available language instances per QID forming the positive set (asymmetric positive sets accommodate QIDs present in only 2-3 languages without dropping them). Minimum language coverage per QID is K_min = 3 languages; QIDs with fewer than 3 language instances are filtered during preprocessing. Class-Aware Masking (CAM) ensures that all instances of the same QID are excluded from the InfoNCE denominator, preventing false-negative contamination. For hard negative mining, type-aware stratification ensures ~50% of in-batch negatives share the anchor entity's Wikidata type (e.g., Q5/human, Q515/city, Q4830453/organization) — forcing the model to discriminate on fine-grained entity identity rather than coarse type. This is implemented via Wikidata instance-of (P31) properties, grouping entities into 8-10 macro-types for sampling. The remaining ~50% are random negatives for diversity. Batch composition is balanced across script families to ensure cross-script contrastive signals appear in every batch. The InfoNCE loss for entity e with QID q is: L_entity(q) = -log[exp(sim(h_q^i, h_q^j)/τ) / (exp(sim(h_q^i, h_q^j)/τ) + Σ_{k≠q} exp(sim(h_q^i, h_k)/τ))], where h_q^i, h_q^j are entity representations from different languages for the same QID, and h_k are representations from different QIDs, with τ = 0.07 as the temperature (tuned in Phase 0 over {0.05, 0.07, 0.1}).
27	
28	**5. Joint Optimization with Gradient Monitoring.** The joint objective is L_total = L_NTP + λ * L_entity_contrastive, with λ initialized at 0.1 (following guidance from headless LM work showing λ ∈ [0.01, 0.1] is appropriate for contrastive + generation joint training during CPT). A potential tension exists: NTP learns language-specific token distributions while contrastive loss pulls entity representations together across languages. Unlike Liu & Niehues' alternating approach, EACA uses joint optimization to ensure entity alignment co-adapts with the language modeling objective — but addresses gradient conflict risk through three mechanisms: (a) Phase 0 gradient analysis: cosine similarity between ∇L_NTP and ∇L_entity_contrastive is computed every 100 steps on the shared LoRA parameters. If gradient cosine similarity is negative for >30% of monitored steps, PCGrad projection (Yu et al., NeurIPS 2020) is applied — projecting the contrastive gradient onto the normal plane of the NTP gradient to eliminate destructive interference. (b) GradNorm (Chen et al., ICML 2018) is implemented as an optional dynamic λ adjustment mechanism: if the gradient magnitude ratio between the two losses drifts beyond 10:1, GradNorm normalizes to equalize learning rates. (c) λ warmup: contrastive loss weight ramps linearly from 0 to λ_target over the first 10% of training steps, allowing NTP to stabilize before contrastive pressure is introduced. Phase 0 reports gradient conflict frequency, cosine similarity distribution, and whether PCGrad/GradNorm activation was required — this informs the full training configuration. If gradient conflicts are severe (>50% of steps) even with PCGrad, the fallback is alternating optimization (NTP steps → contrastive steps per batch) following Liu & Niehues' validated approach.
29	
30	Catastrophic forgetting is mitigated through three mechanisms: (a) LoRA (rank 64) applied to middle layers only (layers 10-22), following CCL-XCoT's selective layer approach and ELO's findings that first/last layers are critical for general capabilities; (b) 15% general-domain English replay data mixed into training batches; (c) cosine learning rate schedule with linear warmup (peak LR 2e-5). Language selection follows a tiered strategy: Tier 1 comprises 4 anchor languages (EN/ZH/JA/DE, >1M entity-fact pairs), Tier 2 includes 6 mid-resource languages (AR/HI/TR/ID/VI/TH, 100K-1M pairs), and Tier 3 covers 3 low-resource languages (SW/YO/KM). Tier 3 viability assessment based on Wikipedia article counts (SW: ~117K, YO: ~37K, KM: ~12K) and FactNet's 0.36 low-resource yield rate estimates approximately 50K-200K entity-fact pairs for Swahili, 15K-60K for Yoruba, and 5K-25K for Khmer. None of the Tier 3 languages are covered by DaMuEL, so all three rely on the Wikipedia wikilinks extraction pipeline (Stage 2 above). A mandatory FactNet coverage audit in Phase 0 will report exact entity-fact pair counts for all 13 languages; minimum viable threshold is set at 10K entity-fact pairs per language (sufficient for contrastive batching at size 128-256 with adequate negative diversity). If any Tier 3 language falls below threshold, contingency replacements include Bengali (BN, ~157K Wikipedia articles), Tagalog (TL, ~115K articles), or Hausa (HA, ~8K articles but stronger NLP benchmark coverage). Languages below 25K pairs receive LEIA-style English entity augmentation to supplement contrastive pairs.
31	
32	Phase 0 pilot uses 500M tokens across 5 languages (3 Tier-1 + 2 Tier-2, selected to span at least 3 scripts for script barrier analysis) for approximately 130 H100 hours, with baselines including: (a) CCL-XCoT-style sentence-level contrastive CPT, (b) Liu & Niehues-style middle-layer sentence-level contrastive alignment (the closest methodological comparison, testing entity-level vs. sentence-level at the same middle layer), (c) LEIA-style entity augmentation without contrastive loss, (d) standard CPT, and (e) KBioXLM-style entity masking adaptation (masking [ENT]-bounded tokens and predicting via NTP, without contrastive loss — testing contrastive vs. masking-based entity alignment on decoders). Phase 0 additionally includes: a layer sweep (layers 12, 14, 16, 18, 20) to empirically determine optimal entity extraction depth; gradient conflict analysis (cosine similarity monitoring, PCGrad activation rate); and script-grouped entity alignment analysis (same-script vs. cross-script gains). Go/no-go criteria require entity cosine similarity improvement of at least 0.05, BMLAMA-53 consistency improvement of at least 2 points, no TyDiQA degradation beyond 1 point, AND gradient conflict rate below 50% (with or without PCGrad). Full training processes 1.5-2.5B tokens on LLaMA-3.1-8B (primary) and Gemma-7B (secondary, for CCL-XCoT comparability) across all 13 languages. A complementary EACA+DCO experiment tests whether pretraining-time and post-hoc consistency methods yield cumulative gains. Evaluation covers BMLAMA-53, TyDiQA-GoldP, X-CODAH, LiveCLKTBench, and CLiKA's XRR metric (to directly measure conductivity improvement), plus entity representation cosine similarity analysis. All metrics are reported with script-grouped breakdowns (same-script pairs, cross-script pairs, overall) as a mandatory analysis dimension. Ablations cover: entity-level vs. sentence-level contrastive (the central hypothesis), contrastive vs. masking-based entity alignment (EACA vs. KBioXLM-style adaptation), EACA vs. EACA+transliteration augmentation (script barrier mitigation), frequency weighting on/off, type-aware vs. random negatives, number of languages, layer selection, joint vs. alternating training, gradient conflict mitigation (none vs. PCGrad vs. GradNorm), contrastive pair construction (FactNet-grounded vs. parallel-text-based), and K_min language threshold (2 vs. 3 vs. 5).
